summary: Dehydration happens when the body loses more fluid than it takes in. Watch for reduced urination, dizziness, unusual sleepiness, or inability to drink.
High blood pressure often has no obvious symptoms. Regular measurement and clinician-guided treatment help reduce long-term risk.
Vaccines protect children and communities from serious infectious diseases. Keep the child's vaccination record and follow the local schedule.
Seek urgent clinical advice for heavy bleeding, severe abdominal pain, severe headache with visual changes, seizures, difficulty breathing, or reduced fetal movement when applicable.

topic: danger signs in a sick child
summary: Take a child to a health facility immediately if they cannot drink or breastfeed, vomit everything, have convulsions, or are unusually sleepy or hard to wake. Fast breathing or the lower chest pulling in with each breath also needs urgent care.
source: WHO, Integrated Management of Childhood Illness (IMCI) chart booklet

summary: A newborn needs urgent care if they are not feeding well, have convulsions, breathe fast, have chest indrawing, feel hot or unusually cold, or have yellow palms and soles.

Give oral rehydration solution (ORS) after each loose stool and zinc as advised by a health worker. Keep breastfeeding and feeding. Seek care quickly if there is blood in the stool, the child cannot drink, or the child is very sleepy.
source: WHO and UNICEF, ORS and zinc guidance

summary: During dengue, seek urgent care for severe abdominal pain, repeated vomiting, bleeding from gums or nose, blood in vomit or stool, unusual sleepiness or restlessness. Drink plenty of fluids. Avoid aspirin and ibuprofen unless a clinician advises them.
source: WHO, Dengue guidelines for diagnosis, treatment, prevention and control

summary: Fever with chills in an area with malaria should be tested the same day with a rapid test or blood smear. Early treatment prevents severe malaria.

topic: cough for more than two weeks
summary: A cough lasting more than two weeks, especially with fever, weight loss, night sweats or blood in the sputum, should be tested for tuberculosis. Testing and treatment are free at government health facilities in India.
Rest and drink fluids. See a health worker if fever lasts more than three days, or sooner if there is a stiff neck, rash, confusion, difficulty breathing, or the person is very weak.

Check blood sugar as advised and look after the feet daily. Sweating, shaking and confusion can mean low blood sugar: if the person is awake and can swallow, give sugar or a sweet drink and seek care.
In hot weather drink water often, avoid heavy work at midday, rest in shade, and check on older people and young children.
source: WHO, Heat and health fact sheet

summary: Stress, low mood and anxiety are common and treatable. Tele-MANAS on 14416 offers free mental health support in Indian languages.
source: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, Tele-MANAS
